    Docs/Get started

    Getting started

    Install, onboarding, open an agent session, add a model, shortcuts

    Nomi: One place. Every AI capability. Run Claude Code and Codex in parallel on one board. Connect a model once — official APIs, third-party, or local. No Nomi cloud account. No edits to those CLIs' global config. The desktop character is optional. Turn it off if you don't want it.

    #Install

    Download the installer for your system from GitHub Releases (<version> is the Release version):

    SystemInstaller
    macOS · Apple Silicon (M-series)Nomi-<version>-arm64.dmg
    macOS · IntelNomi-<version>.dmg
    Windows 10+ (x64)Nomi-Setup-<version>.exe
    Linux (x64)Nomi-<version>.AppImage
    Linux (x64, Debian / Ubuntu)nomi_<version>_amd64.deb

    Linux AppImage: chmod +x Nomi-<version>.AppImage && ./Nomi-<version>.AppImage.

    The macOS build is signed but not notarized. If macOS says Nomi “is damaged”, move it into Applications, then run sudo xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Nomi.app. If Windows shows SmartScreen, click “More info → Run anyway”.

    #First-run onboarding

    On first launch the workbench-sized chat window opens with the guide covering the whole window. The three steps are language and look → AI (agents and a chat model) → personal; the last two can be skipped. Skip from the corner. When it ends, Nomi opens the board if an agent is installed (the empty board's primary action is to dispatch Claude Code or Codex); otherwise it stays in chat and the sidebar's Get started card picks up from there. Rerun it later from Settings → General → Getting started guide → Reopen.

    • AI · Agents: checks whether Claude Code and Codex are installed. Installed ones get a check mark; for the others, Install installs right away, as in Settings → Models & Agents → Agents; a dialog appears only when something blocks the install, such as a missing Node.js or no write permission. Agents sign in with their own accounts, so dispatching them does not need a Nomi model.
    • AI · Chat model (optional): collapsed until you click Connect a model. Pick a third-party provider (a preset or a custom address), enter the key and check & save; the model list stays greyed out until then, and the model you click becomes Nomi's chat model. Open full model settings ends the guide and jumps to Settings → Models & Agents. You can dispatch agents without a model.
    • Personal (optional): name, occupation and interests. Whatever you fill in is saved when the guide ends, even if you skip it; untouched answers are left as they were.
    • Occupation and interests drive the recommendations: the sidebar's Get started card suggests agents (Claude Code and Codex for developers, at least Codex for everyone else) and features (knowledge base, reminders, voice, importing MCP and skills), and the welcome screen's example questions change to match.
    • Startup mode: the guide always opens the main window and keeps the desktop character off. If you want the desktop character, turn it on in Settings → General → Startup & windows.
    • Voice is not part of onboarding: the default is Edge online read-aloud (Xiaoyi, rate -5%) with Read AI replies aloud on; offline, Nomi just shows text. See Voice.

    #Connect a model

    Pick one:

    • Cloud model: Settings → Models & Agents → Third-Party Providers. Add a preset (e.g. DeepSeek, Kimi, OpenRouter) or a custom address, enter an API key and check & save, then pick Nomi's chat model under Task & Cost Routing. See Providers & models.
    • Local model: Ctrl/⌘+Shift+J (Settings → Models & Agents → Local Models), download a recommended small model and start it; it registers as a provider automatically. See Local models.

    #Unified workspace & direct CLI base

    All conversations and projects live in one unified sidebar. When local agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok, dsh, Kimi Code, MiniMax Code) are installed, agent sessions, endpoint filters, and the side workspace appear automatically. You can pick an installed official CLI directly per conversation inside main chat, or expand the multi-tab side workspace for Diff review, files, run traces, and a built-in terminal; see Agents. Terminal and IDE sessions on the Agent Board remain read-only.

    #Common shortcuts

    ShortcutAction
    Ctrl/⌘+KCommand palette (search all actions & settings)
    Ctrl/⌘+NNew chat
    Ctrl/⌘+LFocus input
    Ctrl/⌘+,Open settings
    F2 (hold)Push-to-talk

    Full list and remapping: Personalization.

    #Tray menu

    From the system tray you can: open AI chat, switch the chat model, open model settings, open desktop abilities (file grants / activity log), trigger nomi's motions, open interaction settings (click-through / gravity / stroll), or quit.
